sentences.text: The instant criminal misc. petition has been filed by the petitioner against the order dated 01.02.2021 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge No.5, Kota whereby the revision filed by the petitioner for conversion of the process has been dismissed and the order passed by the learned Magistrate has been affirmed.
Brief facts of the case is that the petitioner was facing the trial under Section 7 read with 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
Owing to some inevitable circumstances, he failed to appear before the trial court and therefore his bail bonds were forfeited and thereafter on 21.07.2018 he has been declared absconder.

The petitioner has moved an application under Section 70(2) of the Cr.P.C. for the conversion of warrant of arrest into bailable warrant but the same has been dismissed by the learned ACJM No.2 Kota vide order dated 07.01.2021.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is ready and willing to appear before the Court but apprehends (2 of 2) [CRLMP-2512/2021] that in the event of surrender before the Ravindra Singh Son Of Daljeet Singh vs State Of Rajasthan on 6 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46850119/

sentences.text: Court, he shall be taken into custody, he is a poor person and the responsibility of the entire family is upon him.
If he would be kept behind the bars, the entire family would be starving.

Counsel further submits that the petitioner assured that henceforth he shall not impede the smooth trial and would regularly appear before the trial Court, physically or through his counsel, if one opportunity is granted to him.
The offence is exclusively triable by the Magistrate and trial is pending since last 20 years, therefore no useful purpose would be served by keeping him behind the bars till disposal of the trial.
Heard counsel for the parties and pondered over the issue.

Though this Court is of the firm view that after the bail bonds are forfeited, an application under Section 70(2) Cr.P.C. is not maintainable,
however, in the peculiar facts and circumstances if the case, looking to the length of the trial, the nature and gravity of the allegation and taking humanitarian approach, I deem it appropriate to quash the order dated 07.01.2021 passed by ACJM No. 2, Kota as well as order dated 01.02.2021 passed by revisional Court.
Accordingly, it is directed that the execution of standing warrant of arrest is stayed.
The petitioner shall surrender before the trial Court on or before 15.02.2022.

On his appearance and upon moving a regular bail application, he shall be released on bail subject to the satisfaction of trial Court with the specific condition that in future he shall not impede the process of trial.
The criminal misc. petition is allowed.
The stay petition is disposed of.

(FARJAND ALI),J PREETI VALECHA /26 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
